title.narrative: Community-based strategies for the conservation of mangroves and improvement of rural livelihoods

description.narrative: The Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena biodiversity hotspot, located at the Colombian Pacific coast, is home to a variety of species, including important mangrove areas. The local population is mainly working in agriculture, traditional fishing, shell collection and trade. However, the ecosystem in the project region is threatened by the expansion of agricultural land, the timber industry, urbanization and the effects of climate change. The project empowered four community councils to implement community-based environmental management strategies. In this way, structures and capacities of these councils were strengthened. Additionally, a concept paper for the sustainable use of the mangroves was drafted and partnerships were established with the private sector in order to better protect and monitor the threatened mangrove areas. At the same time the sustainable management of these areas helped to create diversified sources of income for the local population.
